title.narrative: Delivering Legal Aid Services to Iraqi and Palestinian Refugees

description.narrative: The primary development outcome is that Iraqi and Palestinian refugees, and poor Jordanians, will be better able to exercise socialand economic rights through legal empowerment supported by enhanced legal aid services (information/awareness, counseling and representation). This empowerment will have positive impacts on poverty within these communities, as well as on the overall inclusion ofthese communities in terms of service delivery and exercise of rights. In addition, institutional performance by key stakeholders, including civil society organizations and government entities, related to provision of services to refugees will be improved underthe general framework of legal aid services in Jordan.

title.narrative: 1. The number of Iraqi and Palestinian refugees obtaining legal aid services increases due to the increase in the number of legal aid centers and their geographic coverage

comment.narrative: Geographic coverage for areas of high concentration of refugees limited.
Extended services provided in Amman, Madaba and Zarqa; new services established in Balqaa, Irbid and Jerash
Legal aid services now provided in Saifa near Zarqa, through co-location of JCLA attorney. JCLA has conducted an assessment ofCSOs willing to support co-location in additional areas.

title.narrative: 3. The number of persons accessing legal counseling and representation able to exercise their legal rights and/or resolve disputes increases

comment.narrative: 10 legal representation cases and 30 counseling cases per month. Positive results achieved in 75% of cases involving legalcounseling and representation

Since 1 August 2012, 91 cases of legal representation were provided, and 131 consultations were conducted. Thus JCLA is averaging30 cases of legal representation and conducting roughly 42 consultations per month. The gender breakdown of beneficiaries is 69%women and 31% men. Since representation and counseling activities began only in August 2012, it is not yet possible to accuratelyassess positive results. A more thorough assessment will be carried out in March 2013.

title.narrative: 5. More comprehensive understanding of the demand-side of refugees, and poor Jordanians, related to legal aid and other services

comment.narrative: Improved understanding of demand for legal aid services.

Department of Statistics implemented a survey on the justice sector to 5,000 households. JCLA is analyzing results to improveunderstanding of demand. When the automated case management system is in use, JCLA will compile and produce statistics on demand.Fack forms provided beneficiaries of public awareness activities allow for identifying information demands.

title.narrative: 2. Improved capacity of JCLA to provide legal aid services through an enhanced automated case management system that captures the datanecessary for cases involving refugees and an enlarged pro bono

comment.narrative: Only simple automated system exists, which does not allow for recording of all necessary data and does not provide for adequatestatistics to support monitoring, evaluation and advocacy. There is no comprehensive pro bono system.
Automated case management system fully utilized. Pro bono network enlarged.

JCLA has reviewed and amended case management procedures, which serve as the basis for automation. The parameters for thesoftwaresupporting the automation have been developed, ToRs drafted and an RFP for software companies designed. There has been noreal progress on enhancing the pro bono legal network, but discussions are underway with the Jordan Bar Association.

title.narrative: 4. Refugees have increased awareness about legal rights, legal aid services and the mechanisms for accessing both

comment.narrative: Refugees have limited understanding of rights and services, and how to access them
3 public awareness sessions per month, averaging 30-40 participants, at least 80% of beneficiaries attending legal aid awarenesssessions report an increase in awareness during exit interviews

Since 1 August 2012, JCLA has conducted eight public awareness activities for 237 persons (186 women and 51 men), thus averagingaround 79 participants per month. JCLA created awareness/public information campaign for legal aid, which is being furthertailoredtowards refugees. It has also identified target groups and potential partners for awareness campaignsAnd created adatabase of experts (lawyers, experts, community leaders) to conduct awareness sessions
